QUICK FACTS
Need-to-know rules for Hyderabad roads
🏍️ TWO WHEELERS
Helmet mandatory for rider & pillion. Fine: ₹1000 (1st offence). Riding without licence: ₹5000.
🚗 SPEED LIMITS
City roads: 40–50 km/h. Highways: 80 km/h for cars. ORR: 100 km/h max. School zones: 20 km/h.
🍺 DRUNK DRIVING
BAC limit: 30 mg/100ml. Fine: ₹10,000 + up to 6 months imprisonment. Zero tolerance enforced.
📱 MOBILE USAGE
Using phone while driving: ₹5000. Repeat offence: ₹10,000. Even hands-free is restricted while moving.
🚦 SIGNAL JUMPING
Jumping red light: ₹5000 + possible imprisonment. CCTV enforcement active across Hyderabad.
🅿️ NO PARKING
Parking on yellow lines or bus stops: ₹500 + towing charges up to ₹2000 in GHMC zones.
🪑 SEATBELT
Mandatory for all passengers. Fine: ₹1000 per person. Children under 12 must sit in the back seat.
🚸 SCHOOL ZONES
Speed limit 20 km/h near schools from 7–9 AM and 2–4 PM. Traffic wardens deployed.
📝 DOCUMENTS
Always carry: DL, RC Book, Insurance, PUC Certificate. DigiLocker is accepted as valid proof.

ABOUT
Why Traffic Rules Hyd exists

Traffic Rules Hyd is a pixelated, interactive guide to road rules and safety in Hyderabad, Telangana.

Hyderabad's roads handle over 70 lakh vehicles daily. Knowing the rules isn't just legal — it's survival.

From TSRTC routes to ORR flyovers, from Secunderabad junctions to Gachibowli — this guide covers it all.

Built for students, new drivers, and everyday commuters of the City of Pearls. 🏗️

🪧 TRAFFIC SIGNS
MODULE 01 › TRAFFIC SIGNS
Types of Road Signs
Three categories — know them all
🔴 Mandatory Signs
Signs you must obey — circular with red border. Violations carry heavy fines.
Stop
Come to a complete halt at the stop line — no exceptions.
Left Turn Prohibited
No left turn allowed at this junction.
Right Turn Prohibited
No right turn allowed at this junction.
No U-Turn
U-turns are strictly prohibited at this point.
U-Turn Prohibited
Turning around or reversing direction is not allowed.
No Parking
No vehicle may stop or park here at any time.
One Way — Direction Prohibited
Vehicles may not travel against the direction shown.
Overtaking Prohibited
No overtaking or passing of vehicles ahead.
Speed Limit (50 km/h)
Do not exceed 50 km/h from this point onwards.
Trucks Prohibited
Heavy goods vehicles not permitted on this road.
⚠️ Cautionary Signs
Warning signs — triangular with red border. Alert you to hazards ahead on the road.
Left Hand Curve
Sharp left bend ahead — reduce speed and stay left.
Right Hand Curve
Sharp right bend ahead — slow down before the curve.
Roundabout
Roundabout ahead — give way to traffic from the right.
Pedestrian Crossing
Zebra crossing ahead — yield to waiting pedestrians.
School Ahead
School zone — reduce to 25 km/h during school hours.
Slippery Road
Slippery surface ahead — avoid harsh braking or steering.
ℹ️ Informatory Signs
Blue rectangular signs — guide drivers to hospitals, fuel, parking, and directions.
Destination Sign
White background — shows distances and directions to towns/cities ahead.
Eating Place
Restaurant or food facility ahead — blue rectangular sign with fork & spoon.
Hospital
Medical facility ahead — helps drivers locate emergency healthcare quickly.
Petrol Pump
Fuel station ahead and direction — blue sign with arrow showing which way to turn.
Place Identification
Announces the name of the locality or town you are entering.
Resting Place
Rest area or lay-by ahead — suitable for stopping, stretching or sleeping.

🌧️ MONSOON DRIVING
Monsoon Driving in Hyderabad
June to October — what you need to know to stay safe
🚫 Rule 1 — Waterlogged Roads
  • If water is above ankle height, do not drive through it
  • Above knee level, your engine will stall — you could be swept away
  • Hyderabad underpasses can flood in under 10 minutes during heavy rain
  • When in doubt, turn around — no destination is worth your life
⚡ Rule 2 — Dangerous Underpasses
  • Known flood hotspots: Durgam Cheruvu, Mehdipatnam, Punjagutta, Nampally, Kukatpally
  • Check GHMC flood alerts on Twitter / WhatsApp before travelling
  • Never enter an underpass if you can't see the far end clearly
  • If you stall inside a flooded underpass, abandon the vehicle and move to high ground immediately
🚗 Rule 3 — Speed & Visibility
  • Reduce your speed by at least 50% in heavy rain
  • Switch on headlights — not hazard lights while the car is moving
  • Keep double your normal following distance
  • Wet roads double braking distance — don't tailgate
🌊 Rule 4 — Hydroplaning
  • Happens when tyres lose contact with the road on a wet surface
  • Do not brake hard or steer sharply — this makes it worse
  • Ease off the accelerator and steer gently straight
  • Wait until you feel the tyres grip the road again before steering
  • Most common above 60 km/h — slow down in rain
🏍️ Rule 5 — Two-Wheeler Riders
  • Waterlogged roads hide open manholes — leading cause of monsoon deaths in Hyderabad
  • Ride in the centre of the lane, not near the kerb where water pools
  • Avoid painted road markings — they are extremely slippery when wet
  • Reduce speed before any drain or dip in the road

💸 E-CHALLAN GUIDE
E-Challan — What It Is & How to Pay
Everything you need to know about traffic challans in Hyderabad
📋 What is a Challan?
A challan is an official traffic violation notice issued by the police when you break a traffic rule — like jumping a signal, speeding, riding without a helmet, etc. It's essentially a court summons combined with a fine notice.

An E-Challan (Electronic Challan) is the digital version. Hyderabad Traffic Police use CCTV cameras, speed guns, and handheld devices to issue challans electronically — directly linked to your vehicle's registration number. You don't need to be physically stopped — you may get one without even knowing it at the time.
⚠️ Why You Must Pay
Unpaid challans stack up. All challans are linked to your vehicle registration number in the national database. If you ignore them:
  • Your RC or PUC renewal can be blocked at the RTO
  • The fine amount can escalate with interest
  • The case may be referred to a magistrate court — a warrant notice is sent to your registered address
  • Your driving licence can be suspended for repeated violations
💸 How to Pay Your E-Challan
💸
Pay Your E-Challan Now ↗
echallan.tspolice.gov.in — Official Telangana Police Portal
Open →
Method 1 — Telangana Police Portal
1
Go to echallan.tspolice.gov.in
2
Click Check Challan Status — enter your vehicle number (e.g. TS09EA1234) or challan number
3
View all pending challans. Select the one you want to pay and click Pay Now
4
Pay via UPI, Net Banking, or card. Save your receipt — keep it until the challan clears from records (usually within 3 days)
Method 2 — Parivahan Portal (National)
1
Go to parivahan.gov.in/echallan
2
Enter your vehicle registration number or DL number, then click Check Challan
3
All challans from across India appear here. Pay outstanding Telangana challans directly on this portal
⚠️ If You Don't Pay
Fines accumulate and are tracked against your vehicle. Your RC or PUC renewal can be blocked at the RTO. If referred to court, a warrant notice is issued to your registered address.
✋ Contesting a Wrong Challan
If issued incorrectly (wrong vehicle, CCTV error), appear before the listed court on the hearing date shown in the challan. Bring photos and a written explanation. No fee to contest.

🎒 WHAT TO CARRY
What to Carry on the Road
Required documents by driver type — know what a traffic officer can ask for
✅ Every Driver — Always Carry These
Your official government permit to drive on public roads. Issued by the RTO after passing a theory test + driving test. Must match the vehicle category you're driving.
Registration Certificate — proof your vehicle is legally registered with the government. Contains your vehicle number, chassis/engine number, and owner details. Valid 15 years for private vehicles.
Proof your vehicle has at least third-party insurance — mandatory by law. Covers injury/damage to others in an accident. Renew yearly. Fine for no insurance: ₹2,000 (1st offence).
Pollution Under Control certificate — proves your vehicle's exhaust emissions are within legal limits. Done at certified PUC centres (often at petrol pumps). Renew every 6 months. Fine for no PUC: ₹10,000.
💡 PDF scans on your phone are accepted as valid proof. Save a backup offline too.
🚗 Regular Citizen / Car Driver
Private vehicle owner
  • Driving Licence (DL)
  • Registration Certificate (RC Book)
  • Valid 3rd-party insurance
  • PUC Certificate (not expired)
  • Aadhaar / Passport — for identity if asked
Fine for not carrying DL: ₹5,000
🎓 Learner / LL Holder
Still learning to drive
  • Learner Licence (LL) — carry physical copy
  • RC Book of the vehicle being driven
  • Valid insurance for the vehicle
  • PUC Certificate
  • L board displayed on front & rear of vehicle
  • A licensed co-driver must be present in the passenger seat
Driving without co-driver: fine up to ₹5,000
🏍️ Two-Wheeler Rider
Bike / scooter
  • DL valid for two-wheelers (Category: MC)
  • RC Book
  • Insurance & PUC
  • ISI-marked helmet — rider AND pillion both
  • No more than 1 pillion rider
No helmet fine: ₹1,000 + DL suspension possible
🚕 Auto / Cab / Taxi Driver
Commercial passenger vehicle
  • DL with commercial endorsement (Badge)
  • RC Book (commercial registration)
  • Commercial insurance policy
  • PUC Certificate
  • Taxi / Permit badge issued by RTO
  • Fitness Certificate for the vehicle
  • Route permit (if applicable)
Operating without permit: ₹10,000
🚛 Truck / Goods Vehicle Driver
Heavy commercial vehicle
  • HMV / HGV Driving Licence
  • RC Book (goods vehicle)
  • Goods Carriage Permit
  • Insurance & PUC
  • Fitness Certificate
  • Waybill / consignment note for the goods
  • Speed governor certificate (mandatory for trucks)
  • Overloading fine: ₹20,000 + ₹2,000/tonne over limit
🏛️ Govt / Defence Vehicle
Official / exempted vehicle
  • DL (mandatory for all drivers including govt)
  • RC Book or official vehicle allotment letter
  • Insurance (govt vehicles may carry indemnity bond)
  • Official ID / duty pass — for identity verification
  • Defence: carry Movement Order for inter-state travel
Tax exemption does not exempt from traffic law violations.

      ↑ Choose a topic above
      🚨
      Driving Emergencies
      Quick reference — what to do when things go wrong
      🔧 Steering Failure
      Ease off accelerator → brake gently → steer to road edge → hazard lights on → stop and call for help. Do NOT panic.
      🛑 Brake Failure
      Don't panic → foot off accelerator → downshift gear by gear → apply handbrake gradually → steer to road edge.
      💥 Tyre Burst
      Grip wheel firmly → do NOT brake hard → ease off accelerator → let car slow naturally → steer to shoulder.
      🌊 Skidding
      Do NOT brake during a skid → ease off accelerator → steer gently INTO the skid direction → brake softly only after grip returns.
      🌡️ Engine Overheating
      Pull over → turn off AC but keep engine running 1–2 min → turn engine off → do NOT open radiator cap hot → wait 30 min.
      🌑 Headlight Failure at Night
      Hazard lights on → reduce speed → move to road edge → do NOT stop in lane → place warning triangle 50–100m behind.
      🦶 Stuck Accelerator
      Stay calm → shift to NEUTRAL immediately → brake firmly → switch off ignition once stopped. Do NOT shift to Park while moving.
      🌧️
      Special Driving Conditions
      Quick reference — 7 challenging scenarios
      🌧️ Monsoon
      Slow down, more distance, headlights ON, avoid flooded underpasses.
      🌙 Night Driving
      Headlights from dusk, reduce speed, dip beam for oncoming traffic within 200m.
      🏔️ Hill Driving
      Uphill vehicles get priority. Lower gear on slopes. Never brake-ride downhill.
      ⛰️ Curves & Bends
      Slow before the bend, not during. Stay in lane. No overtaking on curves.
      🌫️ Low Visibility
      Low beam only in fog. Reduce speed drastically. Pull over if under 50m visibility.
      🚧 Road Work
      Slow before work zone, follow signs, watch for workers and debris at all times.
      🚶 Heavy Traffic
      Be patient. No zig-zag. Don't block intersections. Never cross median.
      🅿️ Parking Rules
      ← swipe tabs to see all →
      🚫 Where NOT to Park
      🚗
      Never park where traffic is flowing — never on the main carriageway.
      👁️
      Never park where you can't see at least 50 metres in both directions.
      🚧
      Never block another parked vehicle, a sidewalk, crosswalk, pedestrian crossing or road entrance.
      🚌
      Never park at bus bays or bus stops.
      🏨
      Never park near hotel, theatre or public hall entrances when open.
      🔄
      Never park near any intersection or roundabout.
      ⛔
      Never park in unauthorised or no-parking zones.
      🚶
      Never park on a footpath.
      ↔️
      Always park on the left side in the direction of traffic. Check mirrors before opening your door.
      ◼ Parallel Parking
      Park front-to-rear in a line. Space needed: 1.5× the length of your vehicle.
      1
      Slowly reverse into the space, turning the wheel anti-clockwise. Ensure you've cleared the vehicle ahead.
      2
      When you see the outside rear corner of the car in front, turn wheel clockwise. Watch the car behind.
      3
      Bring the vehicle in line with the kerb.
      4
      If not parallel, drive forward to straighten. Wheels must be straight.
      5
      Apply handbrake, shift to 1st or reverse, switch off engine, remove key.
      6
      Always check traffic before opening the car door.
      📐 Angular Parking
      Parking at an angle to the kerb. Common in car parks, malls and shopping areas.
      1
      Check mirrors and shoulder for traffic behind.
      2
      Give the left indicator to signal your intent to park.
      3
      Steer into the space and straighten the wheels.
      4
      Keep equal distance on both sides, apply handbrake, shift gear.
      5
      Exiting: check mirrors and shoulder. Reverse slowly. Extra care for cycles, rickshaws and pedestrians.
      🌙
      Parking at Night
      Park in a lighted area whenever possible.
      If completely dark — turn on parking lights.
      💡 Know Your Indicators
      🔶 Blinking BOTH sides = Hazard warning — vehicle stopped or emergency
      ➡️ Blinking ONE side = Turning or parking intention
      ⚠️ Passing Parked Vehicles
      🚪 Never open a car door without looking — a passing vehicle may be right there.
      👧 A child may run out suddenly from between parked vehicles — always expect the unexpected.
      🛑 Emergency Roadside Stop
      Only stop by the roadside in a genuine emergency. Keep the stop as brief as possible.
      1
      Signal your intent. Check mirrors and blind spot for a clear gap.
      2
      Steer to the side — stop close to the kerb or road edge.
      3
      Switch on four-way hazard lights immediately.
      4
      Apply the handbrake.
      🚫 Never Park Here
      ❌On a footpath
      ❌Near a crossing
      ❌On the main road
      ❌Blocking traffic
      ❌Wrong side of road
      ❌No-parking zone
      🪪
      Driving Licence
      Quick summary — tap ✕ to start the flashcards
      📌
      What is it? A DL is your official government permit to drive on public roads. Issued by the RTO — mandatory for every driver.
      🎂
      Eligibility 16 yrs for gearless 2-wheelers (50cc), 18 yrs for bikes & cars, 20 yrs for commercial vehicles.
      🛣️
      The Process Apply for LL → Pass theory test → Practice 30 days → Take driving test at RTO → Get your DL!
      🏢
      What is an RTO? Regional Transport Office — the government body that issues DLs, registers vehicles, and enforces road laws.
      📝
      LL Test 15 MCQs, 15 minutes, pass at 60%. Covers signs, rules, and traffic laws. Done at the RTO on a computer.
      🚗
      DL Driving Test 2-wheelers: Figure-8 and H-track. 4-wheelers: course with turns and slopes. No foot-down rule on the track!
      📋
      Documents Needed Aadhaar, age proof, photos, Form 1 + Form 2. For DL: also need your valid LL and test appointment. DigiLocker accepted!
      📅
      Validity & Renewal Valid for 20 years or till age 50. After 50, renew every 5 years. Renew online at parivahan.gov.in.
      📄
      Vehicle Registration
      Quick summary — tap ✕ to go back, or dive into the flashcards
      📌
      What is it? Every vehicle must be officially registered with the government before it can be driven. The RC (Registration Certificate) is your proof.
      🛡️
      What's mandatory? Three things: RC (registration), Third-Party Insurance, and a valid PUC Certificate. All three are required by law.
      🔢
      Number plates White = private, Yellow = taxi/commercial, Green = EV, Blue = diplomat, Black = rental. HSRP plates are tamper-proof and mandatory.
      🏢
      Who handles it? The RTO (Regional Transport Office). For new vehicles, the dealer does the registration for you — you just provide your documents.
      ⏳
      Temporary registration New vehicles get a Temporary Registration (TR) valid for ~1 month while the permanent RC is being processed.
      📅
      Validity & renewal Private vehicle RC is valid for 15 years, then renewed every 5 years. Commercial vehicles have shorter cycles.
      🔄
      Selling a vehicle? RC transfer to the buyer is mandatory. If you skip it and the vehicle gets a challan, you could still be held liable.
